meta.titre: Crystallographic Systems and Axes: from axial lengths to Miller indices
meta.sous_theme: Crystal systems, Miller indices and symmetry

sections.contenu_markdown: A student on a field trip picks up a quartz crystal and notices flat, shining faces that always meet at the same angles whatever the size of the crystal. That regular outside shape comes from the orderly inside arrangement of atoms, and crystallographers describe it with three or four imaginary reference lines called crystallographic axes. At Advanced Level you are asked to name a system from axial lengths and angles, to write the Miller indices of a face, to name the form it belongs to, and to count elements of symmetry. Several terms (crystal axis, axis of symmetry, zone, parameter, index) sound alike, so precise definitions are what separate high marks from average ones.

items: A crystal is a solid whose atoms are arranged in a regular repeating pattern, and its faces are plane surfaces.
The angles between corresponding faces of crystals of the same mineral are constant.
A plane of symmetry divides a body into two halves that are mirror images of each other.
The reciprocal of a number $n$ is $1/n$, and the reciprocal of a very large (infinite) number is zero.

sections.titre: Crystallographic axes, the seven systems, parameters and Miller indices
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Crystallographic axes
Crystallographic axes are imaginary reference lines that cross at the centre of the crystal and are used to describe the position of its faces. By convention $a$ points towards the observer, $b$ to the right and $c$ upwards, each with a positive and a negative end. The angle between $b$ and $c$ is $\alpha$, between $a$ and $c$ is $\beta$, and between $a$ and $b$ is $\gamma$.

### The seven crystal systems
| System | Axial lengths | Axial angles | Axes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cubic | $a = b = c$ | $\alpha = \beta = \gamma = 90^\circ$ | 3 |
| Tetragonal | $a = b \neq c$ | all $90^\circ$ | 3 |
| Orthorhombic | $a \neq b \neq c$ | all $90^\circ$ | 3 |
| Hexagonal | $a_1 = a_2 = a_3 \neq c$ | $a_1, a_2, a_3$ lie in one plane at $120^\circ$ to each other; $c$ is at $90^\circ$ to that plane | 4 |
| Trigonal | usually referred to the hexagonal axes; the rhombohedral setting has $a = b = c$ | rhombohedral setting: $\alpha = \beta = \gamma \neq 90^\circ$ | 4 (or 3) |
| Monoclinic | $a \neq b \neq c$ | $\alpha = \gamma = 90^\circ$, $\beta \neq 90^\circ$ | 3 |
| Triclinic | $a \neq b \neq c$ | $\alpha \neq \beta \neq \gamma \neq 90^\circ$ | 3 |

### Parameters and Miller indices
The **parameters** (Weiss parameters) of a face are the distances at which it cuts the axes, written as multiples of the unit lengths, for example $2a : 3b : 6c$. To find the **Miller indices**:
1. write the intercepts as multiples of the unit lengths (parallel to an axis means intercept $\infty$);
2. take reciprocals, so $\infty$ becomes 0;
3. clear fractions by multiplying by the lowest common denominator, then remove any common factor;
4. write the three whole numbers in round brackets, $(hkl)$, with no commas; a negative intercept is shown by a bar over the index.

For $2a : 3b : 6c$ the reciprocals are $\tfrac12, \tfrac13, \tfrac16$, and multiplying by 6 gives $(321)$. The face that cuts each axis at its unit length is the unit face, $(111)$. A face parallel to $c$ has $l = 0$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks which form or solid shape a given face belongs to.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
A **form** is the set of all faces that the symmetry of the crystal makes equivalent. It is written in braces, $\{hkl\}$, whereas one face is written $(hkl)$. The same indices give different forms in different systems.

| Indices | Cubic | Tetragonal |
|---|---|---|
| $\{100\}$ | cube, 6 faces | tetragonal prism, 4 faces (parallel to $c$ and to one horizontal axis) |
| $\{001\}$ | same form as $\{100\}$ | basal pinacoid, 2 faces (top and bottom) |
| $\{111\}$ | octahedron, 8 faces | tetragonal dipyramid, 8 faces |
| $\{110\}$ | rhombic dodecahedron, 12 faces | tetragonal prism, 4 faces (parallel to $c$, cutting $a$ and $b$ equally) |

In the hexagonal system four indices are used, $(hkil)$, with $i = -(h+k)$; for example $(10\bar{1}0)$ is a vertical prism face.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must count or name planes, axes and the centre of symmetry of a crystal of a given system.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
A **plane of symmetry** divides the crystal into two mirror-image halves. An **axis of symmetry** is a line about which the crystal, rotated through $360^\circ$, repeats its appearance 2 times (diad), 3 (triad), 4 (tetrad) or 6 (hexad). A **centre of symmetry** exists when every face has an equal parallel face on the opposite side. The highest-symmetry class of each system has:

| System | Planes | Axes of symmetry | Centre |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cubic | 9 (3 axial, 6 diagonal) | 13 (3 tetrad, 4 triad, 6 diad) | yes |
| Tetragonal | 5 (1 horizontal, 2 axial, 2 diagonal) | 5 (1 tetrad, 2 axial diad, 2 diagonal diad) | yes |
| Orthorhombic | 3 | 3 diad | yes |
| Hexagonal | 7 (1 horizontal, 3 axial, 3 diagonal) | 7 (1 hexad, 6 diad) | yes |
| Trigonal | 3 | 4 (1 triad, 3 diad) | yes |
| Monoclinic | 1 | 1 diad | yes |
| Triclinic | 0 | 0 | yes |

variantes.nom: Look-alike terms and the crystal zone
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to differentiate between crystal zone, crystal axis, axis of symmetry, parameters and Miller indices.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- A **crystallographic axis** is a reference line used to locate faces; an **axis of symmetry** is a line about which the crystal can be rotated to repeat its appearance. The two can coincide (for example the $c$ axis of a tetragonal crystal is also a tetrad) but are different ideas: a monoclinic crystal has three crystallographic axes yet only one diad.
- A **crystal zone** is a set of faces whose lines of intersection (edges) are all parallel; the common direction of those edges is the **zone axis**.
- **Parameters** are the intercepts of a face on the axes in multiples of the unit lengths; **Miller indices** are the reciprocals of those parameters, reduced to the smallest whole numbers.

sections.enonce_markdown: A crystal of the tetragonal system has two faces. Face 1 cuts the axes at $2a$, $4b$ and $1c$. Face 2 cuts $a$ at $1a$ and $b$ at $\tfrac12 b$ and is parallel to $c$. (a) State the relations between the axial lengths and the axial angles of the tetragonal system. (b) Find the Miller indices of each face. (c) State whether the two faces belong to the same form.

etapes.justification: The system is defined by its axes, so the answer must give both lengths and angles.

etapes.action: Write the parameters of Face 1 as intercepts.
etapes.justification: Intercepts are measured in multiples of the unit lengths $a$, $b$, $c$.

etapes.action: Take reciprocals and clear the fractions for Face 1.
etapes.justification: Miller indices are reciprocals of the intercepts, reduced to whole numbers.
etapes.resultat_markdown: $\tfrac12 : \tfrac14 : 1$, multiplied by 4, gives $2 : 1 : 4$; there is no common factor, so Face 1 is $(214)$.

etapes.justification: A face parallel to an axis has an infinite intercept on it and the reciprocal is zero.
Faces belong to the same form only if symmetry can carry one into the other, which requires the same set of indices apart from order and sign (here only $h$ and $k$ may be exchanged).
etapes.resultat_markdown: The indices $\{2,1,4\}$ and $\{1,2,0\}$ contain different numbers, so the faces belong to different forms.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) $a = b \neq c$ with all axial angles equal to $90^\circ$. (b) Face 1 is **$(214)$** and Face 2 is **$(120)$**. (c) They belong to different forms: Face 2 is a vertical face (parallel to $c$), Face 1 cuts all three axes.

items.erreur_markdown: A face cutting the axes at $2a : 3b : 6c$ has Miller indices $(236)$.
items.pourquoi_faux: Miller indices are the reciprocals of the intercepts, not the intercepts themselves.

items.erreur_markdown: A face parallel to the $c$ axis has index $\infty$ on $c$ (for example $(11\infty)$).
items.pourquoi_faux: The intercept is infinite, so its reciprocal, the index, is zero.

items.erreur_markdown: A face cutting the axes at $2a : 4b : 1c$ is written $(\tfrac12\ \tfrac14\ 1)$.
items.pourquoi_faux: Miller indices must be whole numbers. The fractions must be cleared by multiplying by the lowest common denominator.
items.correction_markdown: Multiply $\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 1$ by 4 to get $(214)$. If a common factor is left, divide it out: $(222)$ is written $(111)$.

items.erreur_markdown: A monoclinic crystal has three crystallographic axes, so it has three axes of symmetry.
items.pourquoi_faux: A crystallographic axis is a reference line, not a rotation axis. Symmetry axes must be counted from the shape of the crystal.
items.correction_markdown: A monoclinic crystal of highest symmetry has only **one** diad axis (perpendicular to its single plane of symmetry).

items.erreur_markdown: The tetragonal system has $a = b = c$ because it has a four-fold axis.
items.pourquoi_faux: Equal axial lengths on all three axes describe the cubic system. In the tetragonal system the vertical axis $c$ has a different length.
items.correction_markdown: Tetragonal: $a = b \neq c$, all angles $90^\circ$. Cubic: $a = b = c$, all angles $90^\circ$.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the crystal system for each description. (a) Three axes mutually at $90^\circ$, all of different lengths. (b) Three axes of equal length mutually at $90^\circ$. (c) Three axes of different lengths, two angles $90^\circ$ and one angle not $90^\circ$. (d) Four axes: three equal axes in one plane at $120^\circ$ to each other and a fourth perpendicular to them, with a six-fold axis of symmetry along the fourth.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Orthorhombic** ($a \neq b \neq c$, all angles $90^\circ$).

(b) **Cubic** ($a = b = c$, all angles $90^\circ$).

(c) **Monoclinic** ($\alpha = \gamma = 90^\circ$, $\beta \neq 90^\circ$).

(d) **Hexagonal** ($a_1 = a_2 = a_3 \neq c$; the three equal axes are in one horizontal plane and $c$ is perpendicular to it). Award one mark for each correct name.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Find the Miller indices of faces with these parameters: face A, $3a : 3b : \infty c$; face B, $1a : 2b : 3c$; face C, $-2a : 2b : 2c$. (b) A face has Miller indices $(312)$. Write its parameters as the smallest whole-number ratio of intercepts $a : b : c$.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Face A: reciprocals $\tfrac13, \tfrac13, 0$; multiply by 3 to get $(110)$.

Face B: reciprocals $1, \tfrac12, \tfrac13$; multiply by 6 to get $(632)$.

Face C: reciprocals $-\tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac12$; multiply by 2 to get $(\bar{1}11)$.

(b) Intercepts are the reciprocals of the indices: $\tfrac13 : 1 : \tfrac12$. Multiplying by 6 gives $2 : 6 : 3$.

**A is $(110)$, B is $(632)$, C is $(\bar{1}11)$; the parameters of $(312)$ are $2a : 6b : 3c$.**

items.enonce_markdown: (a) For a cubic crystal of the highest symmetry, state the number of planes of symmetry (axial and diagonal), the number of axes of each kind, whether there is a centre of symmetry, and the total number of elements of symmetry. (b) Do the same for a tetragonal crystal of the highest symmetry. (c) Explain why a monoclinic crystal described with three crystallographic axes has only one axis of symmetry.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Cubic: planes $3 + 6 = 9$ (3 axial, 6 diagonal); axes $3 + 4 + 6 = 13$ (3 tetrad through the centres of opposite faces, 4 triad through opposite corners, 6 diad through the mid-points of opposite edges); 1 centre. Total $9 + 13 + 1 = 23$.

(b) Tetragonal: planes $1 + 2 + 2 = 5$ (1 horizontal, 2 axial, 2 diagonal); axes $1 + 2 + 2 = 5$ (1 tetrad, 2 axial diad, 2 diagonal diad); 1 centre. Total $5 + 5 + 1 = 11$.

(c) The three crystallographic axes are only reference lines chosen to suit the angles and lengths of the faces ($\beta \neq 90^\circ$). Symmetry is a property of the shape: the only rotation that repeats the appearance of a monoclinic crystal is a half-turn about the one axis perpendicular to its mirror plane (the $b$ axis). **Cubic: 9 + 13 + 1 = 23; tetragonal: 5 + 5 + 1 = 11; monoclinic: 1 diad.**

items_markdown:
The seven systems are defined by axial lengths and angles: cubic $a = b = c$ at $90^\circ$; tetragonal $a = b 
eq c$; orthorhombic $a 
eq b 
eq c$; hexagonal with three equal axes at $120^\circ$ plus $c$; monoclinic with $ eta 
eq 90^\circ$; triclinic with no right angle.
Miller indices: intercepts, reciprocals, clear fractions, remove common factors, write $(hkl)$; parallel to an axis means 0, a negative intercept gets a bar.
$(hkl)$ is one face; $\{hkl\}$ is the whole form. The same indices can mean different forms in different systems (cubic $\{111\}$ octahedron, tetragonal $\{111\}$ dipyramid).
A crystallographic axis is a reference line; an axis of symmetry is a rotation axis. Do not confuse them with each other or with the zone axis.
Highest symmetry: cubic 9 planes, 13 axes, centre; tetragonal 5 planes, 5 axes, centre; orthorhombic 3 planes, 3 diad axes, centre; hexagonal 7 planes, 7 axes, centre.
